title: J&K’s mountains need governance that works, not just another policy

ai.summary: The article discusses the need for integrated mountain governance in Jammu and Kashmir, highlighting existing policies and lessons from international examples like the Alpine Convention and Bhutan's tourism model. It emphasizes connecting ecological protection with tourism, infrastructure, and disaster risk management.

facts.claim: Jammu and Kashmir’s mountains are living ecological systems that sustain rivers, springs, forests, agriculture, horticulture, biodiversity and communities
facts.quote: Jammu and Kashmir’s mountains are not simply scenic backdrops for tourism. They are living ecological systems that sustain our rivers, springs, forests, agriculture, horticulture, biodiversity and communities. Their health is inseparable from our economic security.

facts.claim: The proposed Jammu and Kashmir Sustainable Mountain Development Policy (SMDP) 2026 aims to connect ecological protection, tourism, infrastructure, disaster risk and livelihoods
facts.quote: The proposed Jammu and Kashmir Sustainable Mountain Development Policy (SMDP) 2026 offers an opportunity to address these challenges. Its ambition to connect ecological protection, tourism, infrastructure, disaster risk and livelihoods is timely.

facts.claim: Existing policies in Jammu and Kashmir include the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the Water Act, 1974, the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, forest and wildlife safeguards, the J&K State Disaster Management Policy, 2018, and the Tourism Policy, 2020
facts.quote: My review of the existing policy and legal architecture suggests that Jammu and Kashmir is not starting from zero. The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the Water Act, 1974, the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, forest and wildlife safeguards, the J&K State Disaster Management Policy, 2018, and the Tourism Policy, 2020 already provide important foundations.

facts.claim: The Alpine Convention brings together eight Alpine countries and the European Union through a framework convention supported by protocols covering spatial planning, nature conservation, mountain forests, tourism, transport, energy and soil protection
facts.quote: The Alpine Convention is perhaps the strongest example of a coordinated mountain-governance framework. It brings together eight Alpine countries and the European Union through a framework convention supported by protocols covering spatial planning, nature conservation, mountain forests, tourism, transport, energy and soil protection.

facts.claim: Bhutan's tourism model uses a Sustainable Development Fee to support national development and environmental priorities
facts.quote: Bhutan offers a different lesson. Its tourism model has used a Sustainable Development Fee to support national development and environmental priorities.

facts.claim: Nepal’s forest cover increased from 29 per cent in 1994 to more than 46 per cent in 2022 due to community-based forest management
facts.quote: A 2025 World Bank report records a rise in Nepal’s forest cover from 29 per cent in 1994 to more than 46 per cent in 2022, attributing much of the progress to community-based forest management.

ai.background_note: The article emphasizes the need for integrated mountain governance in Jammu and Kashmir, highlighting existing policies and lessons from international examples to address ecological and tourism challenges.
